```python
converted = Decimal(amount_cents) * Decimal(rate)
return int(converted.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
```

It rounds down to the nearest minor unit, following the April 2026 Treasury decision that a conversion should never credit a customer more than the rate allows. That's intentionally different from tax, which uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Negative amounts also round down, so `-999 × 0.9234` gives `-923`. I added a one-line comment explaining why.

**Test fixture problem:** `tests/fxdata.py` looks for a per-day file at `tests/fixtures/fx/2026-09-30.json`. The only fixture there is a monthly CSV, `usd-2026-09.csv`.
